content: #37793 has caused breakage in FLT because there are several instances of a theorem with a @[to_additive] tag being renamed but the additivised lemma not being deprecated. Examples: coe_finsetProd, val_finsetProd, image_finsetProd_pi... . Is it possible to check for such slips in CI nowadays? We have python code which does a first approximation to this but which presumably wouldn't catch this issue. I remember there was talk about upgrading this to Lean code.
That PR was meant to be only whitespace changes. Donyou mean a different PR, or did something else sneak in (can you name one)?
Sorry, had it right in the title and miscopied in the main text. fixed now.
If the number isn't wrong, then see https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/37793#issuecomment-4322313081 and #38550
"Sorry, these extra deprecations are too much work for me, so I will give Kevin extra work instead. bors merge" :-) And thanks Yael for #38550 !

I think we should

  1. Make to_additive handle deprecated aliases (#19424)
  2. Change the script to make it Lean-aware instead of text based, by using a Lean-diff tool that compares against master (there's Leaff but wasn't there a new diff tool planned to replace the autogenerated PR summaries?)

Adding some grep to_additive to the script isn't great IMO. But idk the timeline of the Lean diff tool so maybe it's a fine temp solution.

I don't really understand the conclusion of the discussion here #mathlib4 > to_additive and deprecated alias @ 💬 (it seems to be people saying "do this", "no actually that doesn't work"). What is the thing which #37793 should be doing? Is it more than just adding deprecations for the currently-undeprecated declarations? (Claude wants to know)

WIP PR at #38616, will come back to it in about 10 hours (need to go to work and have run out of Claude credits, but apparently I should be doing the additive versions first and then @[to_additive existing] the multiplicative ones)

Can the new olean-diffing feature help here, by pointing out the missing deprecations? In other words, would a definitely correct way to generate the list of necessary deprecations to be to revert #37793 on current master, and look at the public API changes?

If there is a way of checking that the LLM-generated #38616 has (a) not missed anything and (b) has deprecated the correct names in every case, that would be awesome. Note that there will be one further change to it (when I've finished doing my day job), moving the additive deprecations to before the multiplicative ones and then adding @[to_additive existing, deprecated ...] to the multiplicative ones. This might also catch some errors.

I conjecture that olean-diffing can do this, kind of, by

  • making a PR reverting #37793 and commenting !olean_report at the beginning of a line, and getting a diff of the missing deprecations,
  • commenting the same in #38616,
  • manually commenting the diffs in both PRs.
!olean_report doesn't know about decls, only modules, see the PR description of #38400
Oops, yes --- that was wishful thinking on my part. Sorry!

Snir Broshi said:

(there's Leaff but wasn't there a new diff tool planned to replace the autogenerated PR summaries?)

I agree with that workflow, but I'm unsure of the state of diffing tools. I vaguely remember Damiano Testa mentioning they're working on such a thing? But I'm not sure

I opened a draft PR for the add_deprecations.sh script fix from issue #38550: PR #38635. It handles the common mul/add case conservatively and skips anything that looks like it needs manual attention. I'm here to iterate based on maintainer feedback.

#38616 should be good to go now (assuming it passes CI). The new approach of @[to_additive existing ...] adds a check that we've got the additivistion of the deprecated multiplicative names right. Of course if we're able to revert #37793 and then do this programmatically then that's great -- happy to close #38616 -- but right now my impression is that we might be a few days off this, and #37793 might be breaking other repos as well as FLT.

I have opened #40503 which implements support for deprecations in to_additive.

The new way to deprecate a declaration @[to_additive ...] theorem ... will be to simply add the deprecation before to_additive:
@[deprecated foo (since := "today"), to_additive ...] theorem ...
Based on @Floris van Doorn's suggestion, I've now implemented it so that you have to write @[to_additive (attr := deprecated ...)], which should be more intuitive than how I did it at first.
